item.title: (Solved) EditForm requires either a Model parameter or an EditContext parameter
item.description:
Summary

In this article, we will explore how to resolve the Blazor Server error: EditForm requires either a Model parameter, or an EditContext parameter. We’ll go through a step-by-step explanation of the code, practical examples, and alternative methods to achieve the same functionality.

Understanding the Error

The error EditForm requires either a Model parameter, or an EditContext parameter occurs when Blazor’s EditForm component is not provided with the required parameters for model binding. Let’s examine a simple example that throws this error and then fix it.

item.title: Solved: How to Redirect to a Specific Page After Login in .NET 8 Blazor
item.description:
Redirecting users to a specific page after they log in is a common requirement in applications. In .NET 8 Blazor, especially with ASP.NET Core Identity and the new Blazor templates, implementing this functionality can be straightforward with the right configurations. This guide will walk you through everything you need to know to achieve a seamless post-login redirection to any page, like a user dashboard.

Blazor’s individual account authentication comes with preconfigured login templates, but custom redirection requires specific configurations. Here’s how to set it up effectively.
